subject.title: sessions.patch has no plugin-ownership check, unlike its sessions.delete sibling

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.patch` ownership bypass be fixed through the normal public bugfix path, or routed through security-owned advisory/backport handling first?
rationale: The source evidence supports a narrow code fix, but the affected behavior is a stable gateway plugin-isolation boundary that can mutate another plugin's session state.

options.title: Approve narrow public fix
options.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression tests while maintainers decide release-note or backport wording.

options.title: Route through security handling
options.body: Pause public repair automation and handle advisory, disclosure, and backport decisions through the repository security process.

options.title: Declare the asymmetry intentional
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers explicitly want plugin-runtime callers to patch foreign sessions and can document why delete remains stricter.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow public fix
recommendation.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression tests while maintainers decide release-note or backport wording.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter merged the blamed current-main snapshot and is the strongest available routing owner for a public security-boundary decision.
